jokes.label: Joke A
jokes.title: Just Browsing
jokes.joke: I went into an antiques store telling myself, “I’m just browsing.” Twenty minutes later I was carrying out a Victorian chair I didn’t need because the owner said, “They don’t make them like this anymore.” Apparently my financial weakness is triggered by any object whose manufacturer is dead.

jokes.label: Joke B
jokes.title: My Dietician Has Given Up
jokes.joke: I hired a dietician. Real one, clipboard, disappointed sighs included. First week she catches me eating a donut in the car. Second week, a donut in a different car, like I thought that was the loophole. By week three she just texts me a photo of a salad and writes 'this is what hope looks like.' I told her I respect the hustle, but I've made my choice, and my choice is glazed.

jokes.label: Joke C
jokes.title: Nutrition Consultation
jokes.joke: My dietician told me, 'Whatever you do, don't eat your feelings.' Which sounds great in theory, but when you're having a terrible day, a sleeve of Oreos is just so much better at active listening.

jokes.label: Joke D
jokes.title: Second Snack
jokes.joke: I saw a dietician last week. She mapped out my entire diet, no exceptions. I left her office ready to change my life. Then I stopped for gas and somehow walked out with a king-size candy bar and a bag of chips. I ate them in the car before I even started the engine. Some people get a second wind. I get a second snack the second someone tells me not to.

jokes.label: Joke E
jokes.title: Cheat Day Negotiation
jokes.joke: My dietician told me, "When you're tempted, just ask yourself whether you really need that snack." I'm so weak-willed I treated it like a debate prompt. Twenty minutes later I had a family-size bag of chips and a closing argument: "The defense rests... directly on crumbs."

scores.comment: Strong escalation and stage rhythm; the different-car loophole is the freshest beat, and 'my choice is glazed' lands cleanly.
Clear and concise with a solid personification punchline, but 'eating your feelings' is a familiar setup and the turn is fairly expected.
Competent and understandable, but the structure is conventional and the 'second snack' wordplay is mild rather than a strong final turn.
Good debate-frame escalation with a clean final image; slightly constructed wording, but the closing-argument turn is distinct and effective.
Nice escalation and a genuinely funny closing generalization; clean stage voice.
Solid 'eating feelings' bit; punchline lands but the angle is fairly familiar.
A bit long for the payoff; 'second snack' pun is cute but not a big laugh.
Courtroom conceit is fresh and the crumbs closer is a genuinely good snap.
Solid observational premise with clean escalation. The punchline lands with an amusing, dry turn that feels authentic to stage delivery.
Good stage pacing and vivid imagery, especially switching cars. However, the final punchline fizzles into a familiar diet-standup trope rather than snapping shut.
Follows a very standard setup-and-immediate-relapse arc. The closing line merely re-explains the premise with minor wordplay rather than providing a real twist.

Solid premise and a clean final image, but the close explains more than it snaps.
